transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Sam Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Rodriguez (Nova CTO), Marcus Lee (Lead Eng), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary: quick SDK walkthrough: Python/TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns (API key vs SSO), env setup, demo of streaming chat + embeddings, discussion of dedicated vs hosted for latency/cost, next steps to run perf tests and share security artifacts.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, will keep this focused on SDK integration and quickstarts, sam will jump into the code, and then we can talk infra and security
00:22 Speaker 2 (Elena): great thanks, appreciate it. we just want to validate how fast we can get a proof of concept running, python first then maybe typescript for frontend. our latency budget for UI is around 300ms p50, 800ms p95 for small chat completions
00:40 Speaker 3 (Sam): cool yeah that's helpful. quick qual: where are you planning to run models, hosted or private/dedicated?
00:48 Speaker 4 (Marcus): initially hosted to move fast, but if latency/cost we may look at dedicated pools or private (VPC) later, also need to check data residency for EU customers
01:10 Speaker 2 (Avery): okay perfect. we'll show the quickstart, auth flows (api key env var vs short-lived tokens / sso), and then show how Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching to help cost
01:35 Speaker 3 (Sam): alright jumping into the Python SDK. top-level install is pip install redwood-inference (note: this is the quickstart package name), then set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or use OIDC/SSO for org-level access
01:55 Speaker 3 (Sam): code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.chat.completions.create(model='rw-3b', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]) -- and resp.text or streaming via client.chat.stream(...)
02:22 Speaker 4 (Marcus): quick q, does the SDK handle reconnects/streaming backpressure?
02:30 Speaker 3 (Sam): yes, there is built-in backpressure and automatic retry for transient errors. streaming uses chunked events; you can supply a callback to handle partial tokens. the TS SDK mirrors this apis but import differs: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference' and new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
03:05 Speaker 2 (Avery): note on auth patterns: api key in env is simplest for POC; for enterprise we recommend SAML/SSO + short-lived service tokens via the customer control plane. also we integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrapping for Private installs
03:30 Speaker 3 (Sam): demo time, i'll run the quickstart example in python. starting a small chat, sending 2 messages, measure latency. (typing sounds)
04:10 Speaker 3 (Sam): ok response came back in ~220ms p50 on my local test to a small prompt using rw-3b hosted region us-west-2 -- your mileage will vary depending on prompt length and model choice
04:40 Speaker 4 (Elena): that's promising. for embeddings pipeline, what does the call look like? we plan to embed product descriptions nightly
04:55 Speaker 3 (Sam): embeddings call is client.embeddings.create(model='rw-embed-4k', input=[...]) returns vector arrays. SDK supports batch input arrays and automatic chunking. we also have a streaming bulk upload helper in the TS SDK to POST chunks and get back ids
05:20 Speaker 4 (Marcus): any limits on payload size / sequence length?
05:28 Speaker 3 (Sam): sequence length depends on model, SDK will surface model profile and we have validations: if you exceed, it will error with a helpful message. also recommend prefix caching for system prompts; Redwood runtime does KV cache to reuse key-value cache across requests (sometimes transcripts transcribed as "K V cash" in older notes)
06:00 Speaker 2 (Avery): talking about environment setup: we usually recommend a simple .env file for dev: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION, REDWOOD_ORG_ID (if needed). for production with Dedicated or Private, you wire up an OIDC provider and use short-lived tokens or instance credentials
06:30 Speaker 3 (Sam): quick TS demo: npm i @redwood/inference && import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_API_KEY }); // note for browser usage use server-proxy or ephemeral keys to avoid leaked keys
06:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): got it. for our frontend we plan a server-side proxy to call Redwood from our backend to avoid exposing API keys
07:10 Speaker 3 (Sam): yep that's recommended. also we support function calling and structured output. if you use function-calling, the SDK will parse responses into JSON objects when responses are well-formed but watch out for hallucinations and always validate on your side
07:40 Speaker 2 (Avery): let's talk about costs: for hosted API there's per-token pricing, but Redwood Optimize can analyze your workload and suggest batching and quantization profiles. for example going from 16-bit to int8 quant reduces token cost but may impact quality; Optimize has suggested thresholds per model
08:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): can Redwood Optimize recommend batch sizes automatically? our throughput target is 200 rps for embeddings pipeline at night and 50 rps for interactive chat
08:20 Speaker 3 (Sam): yes the Optimize module can run profiling jobs (you upload sample requests), it will recommend batching/caching settings and expected cost delta and latency impact. note: for hard SLOs Dedicated with reserved capacity is typical because you get predictable throughput and less noisy neighbors
08:50 Speaker 4 (Elena): security and compliance: do you support SOC2 and audit logs and SSO?
09:00 Speaker 2 (Avery): yes SOC 2 Type II, audit logs available in Console, SAML/SSO, RBAC, encryption at rest with KMS integration. we'll share the whitepaper link in the follow-up. for Private we support on-prem and VPC peering and bring-your-own KMS/HSM
09:25 Speaker 3 (Sam): quick note about logs: console has token-level cost breakdown, tracing hooks, and per-route dashboards. logs can be exported to your SIEM via S3 or direct streaming
09:45 Speaker 4 (Marcus): how do we validate latency in our region? can we run a quick benchmark against our sample prompt set?
09:55 Speaker 3 (Sam): absolutely. next step is we provide a benchmark harness - a small script that runs your prompts against hosted and optionally Dedicated pools. we'll need a sample prompt file and target concurrency, we'll run and share numbers in the spreadsheet
10:20 Speaker 4 (Marcus): ok i'll prepare that. one more Q re: model versions and rollouts - how do you pin versions and rollback?
10:30 Speaker 2 (Avery): Console supports model pinning and rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper variants when load spikes. rollout is per-route and you can set failover to a quantized variant or different region
10:55 Speaker 3 (Sam): back to SDK details: environment variable names we use: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL (if using private control plane), REDWOOD_REGION. For TS in browser use short lived keys mounted via backend route: /api/redwood-proxy that exchanges ephemeral token. we have example in quickstart repo: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: link in notes)
11:30 Speaker 4 (Elena): any gotchas on rate limiting? we have spikes during peak sale events
11:40 Speaker 3 (Sam): rate limits are per-account and per-deployment. Console will surface current limits; for Dedicated you can request quota increases. Also built-in automatic backoff and retry in SDK to help smoothing spikes
12:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): how about caching for chat history - to keep costs down?
12:15 Speaker 3 (Sam): prefix/KV caching is the main mechanism; if you're repeating system prompts or long context prefixes, enable prefix caching and we will keep KV cache across sessions for the same conversation id. also partial caching of embeddings is possible for vector lookup pipeline
12:45 Speaker 2 (Avery): for POC you can use hosted, we'll run the perf harness and if numbers look good we'll discuss Dedicated commit levels. i'll include pricing tiers and an example calc for your expected monthly token volume
13:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): curious about private deployment latency differences vs hosted in eu-west-1
13:15 Speaker 3 (Sam): Private on-prem will remove network hop, but you manage infra; Dedicated in a cloud region close to customers often gives best balance. we can run both in parallel for testing if that's useful
13:40 Speaker 4 (Priya): any sample repos for typescript + nextjs integration?
13:50 Speaker 3 (Sam): yes quickstart has nextjs example using server middleware and client streaming. I'll paste the repo link in the follow-up. also we have an official npm package name and pip package in the docs
14:10 Speaker 2 (Avery): small note: if you plan to do on-prem or VPC peering we need your network CIDR and peering windows; Sam will collect that in follow-up if you go that route
14:30 Speaker 3 (Sam): live demo: i'm going to show streaming token callback in TS, code logs showing partial tokens arriving every ~40ms. (screen share noises)
15:20 Speaker 4 (Elena): looks good. do you support structured output enforcement? we want JSON responses for downstream ingestion
15:30 Speaker 3 (Sam): we have function-calling + best-effort schema enforcement, also reranking to validate outputs. but you should still validate on client side. Optimize can also surface regression alerts tied to eval sets
16:00 Speaker 2 (Avery): let's capture action items: we'll send pricing + tentative Dedicated tiers, Sam will share benchmark harness and quickstart links, and Marcus will provide prompt set.
16:20 Speaker 4 (Marcus): noted. one more thing - encryption keys: for private we'd like to use our own KMS. is that supported?
16:30 Speaker 2 (Avery): yes bring-your-own KMS is supported for Private, and we support HSM integrations for enterprise. details in security pack we'll send
16:55 Speaker 3 (Sam): practical quickstart tips: enable debug logging in SDK with REDWOOD_DEBUG=true to see request/response headers, and use the sample docker-compose for local testing if you want to emulate Private endpoints
17:20 Speaker 4 (Elena): timeline discussion: we'd like a POC within 3 weeks and decide on Dedicated by end of quarter
17:35 Speaker 2 (Avery): that sounds feasible; next step we'll aim to get perf numbers in a week from you and we'll follow up with a SE run for deeper perf checks
17:50 Speaker 4 (Priya): ok thanks everyone, helpful session.
18:05 Speaker 1 (Avery): thanks all. i'll email the links and pricing after this call.

Transcript notes/disfluencies: occasional mis-transcripts (e.g., K V cash instead of KV cache), some tech terms spelled out differently (SAML vs saml), small pauses and crosstalk.
